gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the MacBook Air only fast-charges from a 70 W or higher USB PD source (Apple) and takes in about 71 W at most (ChargerLAB, 15-inch M2 Air), so what decides the pick is whether the laptop output stays at 70 W or more once a phone is plugged in: the UGREEN 130W keeps 100 W on USB-C1, while the Baseus FC41 20K 100W drops to 65 W.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's UGREEN 130W review (cited) and both Best Batteries pages' review (in the results, not cited); us.ugreen.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so the cited maker page was not read. Macworld gives the UGREEN port split (100 W + 30 W, 15 W shared with three devices) and 56% in 30 minutes on a MacBook Air M3; Best Batteries gives the same split, a thermal step-down to 65 W at 34% left under a constant 100 W load, and 54.8-64.7 Wh delivered. Neither states Apple's 70 W fast-charge line, the Air's own intake ceiling, any rival bank's split, or the cable current limit. Part of the mechanism (the UGREEN split and step-down) is already there, so this is 2, not 3.
decides: Confirms the UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130W as the pick: its USB-C1 stays at 100 W with a phone on USB-C2 (Macworld), above Apple's 70 W line, and Macworld measured 56% in 30 minutes on an Air M3. The Baseus FC41 20K 100W wins only the built-in-cable, laptop-alone segment: Notebookcheck reports one cable at up to 65 W with the other three outputs sharing 15 W once several devices are connected, which is under Apple's 70 W line. A 130 W or 140 W rating adds nothing for the Air itself, since ChargerLAB saw about 71 W from Apple's 96 W and 140 W adapters. One caveat for the page: Best Batteries saw the UGREEN fall to 65 W at 34% left under a constant 100 W load, so the last third of the bank may not fast-charge.
candidates: Baseus EnerFill FC41 Digital Display Power Bank 20000mAh 100W

findings.label: MacBook Air (M5) fast-charge requirement, Apple's words
findings.value: "Fast-charge capable with 70W or higher USB PD power source"; 13-inch battery 53.8 Wh, 15-inch 66.5 Wh; in the box: "40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max"
findings.note: The page covers the Apple M5 models, both sizes. The included adapter tops out at 60 W, so the Air does not fast-charge from its own charger.

findings.label: Apple's fast-charge adapter list for MacBook Air (2022 or later)
findings.value: 140 W, 96 W or 70 W USB-C Power Adapter with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable or USB-C charge cable; 67 W on 13.6-inch models only; "up to 50 percent in around 30 minutes"
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Page shows Published Date November 05, 2026. It names no third-party adapters or power banks; the only third-party item is a display "capable of delivering 85W". A 65 W port is below every listed option.

findings.label: MacBook Air maximum charging input, measured
findings.value: About 71 W from Apple's 96 W and 140 W adapters; limited to 70 W on a 70 W charger and 35 W on the 35 W charger
findings.source_title: Charging Review of New Apple 15-inch MacBook Air (A2941) - ChargerLAB
findings.note: ChargerLAB, published July 5, 2023, on the 15-inch Air A2941 (2023 model): "We tried Apple 96W and 140W, the power is only about 71W, which should be the maximum input power of this laptop." On the 70 W charger the peak was about 67 W at 35 minutes and a full charge took 2 h 19 min. This is not a measurement of the M4 or M5 Air.

findings.label: USB-C cable power classes (USB-IF)
findings.value: Every USB-C to USB-C cable must be labelled 60 W or 240 W; a 60 W cable is one "that supports 20V at 3A"
findings.note: Arithmetic: 70 W at 20 V is 3.5 A, which is over the 3 A of a 60 W cable, so a 60 W cable holds a 100 W port to 60 W at 20 V, under Apple's 70 W line. The 3.5 A figure and the 60 W cap are my inference from the cable class; the USB-IF page does not say that a 5 A cable is required. A bank with a built-in 100 W cable avoids the question.

findings.label: Port split with a second and third device
findings.value: USB-C1 100 W + USB-C2 30 W = 130 W with two devices; with three devices USB-C2 and USB-A are throttled to a shared 15 W
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld: "the USB-C1 alone can output a maximum of 100W and the USB-C2 30W." The laptop port stays at 100 W with a phone on USB-C2.

findings.label: MacBook Air charge in 30 minutes, measured
findings.value: 56% on a MacBook Air M3 from USB-C1
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld's measurement; the review does not say whether the Air was 13- or 15-inch. It beats Apple's "up to 50 percent in around 30 minutes". The box includes a short charging cable whose rating Macworld does not give.

findings.label: Output step-down and delivered energy, measured
findings.value: Fell to 65 W with 34% of charge left, after about 22 min of a constant-load test; 54.8 Wh delivered at 100 W, 54.8-64.7 Wh depending on the power drawn
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Best Batteries calls the cause thermal and says the allocation between ports is fixed. It also reports 45 W "until the end" in a test on two real laptops, which it does not name. No test at the Air's roughly 70 W draw was found. This page was already in ChatGPT's results.

findings.product: Baseus EnerFill FC41 Digital Display Power Bank 20000mAh 100W
findings.label: Port split with several devices connected
findings.value: "one USB-C cable offers up to 65W, with the remaining three outputs sharing 15W"; alone, each USB-C cable and the USB-C port give up to 100 W; 65 W input; 15.1 oz (~428 g)
findings.source_title: Baseus releases new 20K power bank with display in US - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck (Polly Allcock, 2025-11-13, updated 2026-02-17), a news report of Baseus's figures, not a bench test. 65 W is under Apple's 70 W fast-charge line, so the Air fast-charges from this bank only when nothing else is plugged in. baseus.com returned HTTP 429 today, so this was not checked on the maker's page.
